arxiv-1905-04603.title: A New Stock Market Valuation Measure with Application to Retriement Planning
arxiv-1905-04603.creator: Andrey Sarantsev
arxiv-1905-04603.description: Abstract . We generalize the classic Shiller cyclically adjusted price-earnings ratio (CAPE) used for prediction of future total returns of the stock market. We treat earnings growth as exogenous. The difference between log wealth and log earnings is modeled as an autoregression of order 1 with linear trend 4.6% and Gaussian innovations. Detrending gives us a new valuation measure.

arxiv-2101-11190.title: Boost-S : Gradient Boosted Trees for Spatial Data and Its Application to FDG-PET Imaging Data
arxiv-2101-11190.creator: Reza Iranzad, Xiao Liu, W. Art Chaovalitwongse, Daniel S. Hippe, Shouyi Wang, Jie Han, Phawis Thammasorn, Chunyan Duan, Jing Zeng, Stephen R. Bowen
arxiv-2101-11190.description: Abstract Boosting Trees are one of the most successful statistical learning approaches that involve sequentially growing an ensemble of simple regression trees (i.e., “weak learners”). This paper proposes a new gradient Boost ed Trees algorithm for S patial Data (Boost-S) for spatially correlated data with covariate information.

arxiv-2101-12506.title: Learning User Preferences in Non-Stationary Environments
arxiv-2101-12506.creator: Wasim Huleihel Soumyabrata Pal Ofer Shayevitz
arxiv-2101-12506.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wasim Huleihel Soumyabrata Pal Ofer Shayevitz. Recommendation systems often use online collaborative filtering (CF) algorithms to identify items a given user likes over time, based on ratings that this user and a large number of other users have provided in the past. This problem has been studied extensively when users’ preferences do not change over time (static case); an assumption that is often violated in practical settings.

arxiv-2108-13632.title: On negative spheres in elliptic surfaces
arxiv-2108-13632.creator: András I. Stipsicz, Zoltán Szabó
arxiv-2108-13632.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by András I. Stipsicz, Zoltán Szabó. Using elliptic fibrations with specific singular fibers, we find spheres with very negative self-intersections in elliptic surfaces and in their blow-ups. Introduction Suppose that X is a simply connected, closed, smooth, oriented four-manifold. As H_{2}\cong\pi_{2} in this case, all second homology classes can be represented by a smooth map f\colon S^{2}\to X , and in this dimension we can assume that f is an immersion.

arxiv-2204-13253.title: Temporal Analysis of Transaction Ego Networks with Different Labels on Ethereum
arxiv-2204-13253.creator: Baoying Huang 1 , Jieli Liu 2 , Jiajing Wu 1 4 , Quanzhong Li 1 , Hao Lin 3
arxiv-2204-13253.description: Abstract Due to the widespread use of smart contracts, Ethereum has become the second-largest blockchain platform after Bitcoin. Many different types of Ethereum accounts (ICO, Mining, Gambling, etc.) also have quite active trading activities on Ethereum. Studying the transaction records of these specific Ethereum accounts is very important for understanding their particular transaction characteristics, and further labeling the pseudonymous accounts.

arxiv-2301-04561.title: Confining QCD theory and Mass Gap
arxiv-2301-04561.creator: V. Gogokhia, G.G. Barnafoldi
arxiv-2301-04561.description: Abstract The novel constraint on any solution to QCD has been exactly and uniquely derived in the framework of the the Slavnov-Taylor identities for the gauge particles propagators. It has the two independent solutions. 1). The first one leads to the general QCD, possessing the confinement phase transition. 2).

arxiv-2309-01045.title: Exploring the Structures and Substructures of the Andromeda Satellite Dwarf Galaxies Cassiopeia III, Perseus I, and Lacerta I ODI-PPA ( Gopu et al. 2014 ) , QuickReduce pipeline ( Kotulla 2014 ) , DAOPHOT ( Stetson 1987 ) , ALLFRAME ( Stetson 1994 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 )
arxiv-2309-01045.creator: Katherine L. Rhode, Nicholas J. Smith, Denija Crnojevic, David J. Sand, Ryan A. Lambert, Enrico Vesperini, Madison V. Smith, Steven Janowiecki, John J. Salzer, Ananthan Karunakaran, Kristine Spekkens
arxiv-2309-01045.description: Abstract We present results from wide-field imaging of the resolved stellar populations of the dwarf spheroidal galaxies Cassiopeia III (And XXXII) and Perseus I (And XXXIII), two satellites in the outer stellar halo of the Andromeda galaxy (M31). Our WIYN pODI photometry traces the red giant star population in each galaxy to ∼ \sim 2.

arxiv-2311-04236.title: Distributed Agent-Based Collaborative Learning in Cross-Individual Wearable Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition
arxiv-2311-04236.creator: Ahmad Esmaeili, Zahra Ghorrati, Eric T. Matson
arxiv-2311-04236.description: Abstract The rapid growth of wearable sensor technologies holds substantial promise for the field of personalized and context-aware Human Activity Recognition. Given the inherently decentralized nature of data sources within this domain, the utilization of multi-agent systems with their inherent decentralization capabilities presents an opportunity to facilitate the development of scalable, adaptable, and privacy-conscious methodologies.

arxiv-2602-08974.title: Cyclic universe from uniform rate inflation on the brane with a timelike extra dimension
arxiv-2602-08974.creator: Rikpratik Sengupta, Arkajit Aich, Kaushik Bhattacharya
arxiv-2602-08974.description: Abstract We investigate a non-singular cosmological scenario in which uniform-rate inflation is realised on an anisotropic Shtanov-Sahni braneworld. The model naturally resolves the initial singularity resulting in an infinite number of smooth non-singular bounces, while accommodating a phase of accelerated expansion driven by a scalar field rolling at a constant rate.

pmc-10522977.title: A high-throughput protocol for deamination of long single-stranded DNA and oligo pools containing complex sequences
pmc-10522977.creator: Yanyan Wang, Senxin Zhang, Xiaoqi Zheng, Leng-Siew Yeap, Fei-Long Meng
pmc-10522977.description: SummaryCytidine deaminases as DNA mutators play important roles in immunity and genome stability. Here, we present a high-throughput protocol for deamination of long single-stranded (ss) DNA or oligo pools containing complex sequences. We describe steps for the preparation of both enzyme (activation-induced deaminase, AID) and ssDNA substrates, the deamination reaction, uracil-friendly amplification, and data analysis.

pmc-10641250.title: Nest desertion as an anti-parasitism strategy in hosts selects for late egg-laying behavior in cuckoos
pmc-10641250.creator: Guo Zhong, Guixia Wan, Yuhan Zhang, Huahua Zhao, Longwu Wang, Wei Liang
pmc-10641250.description: SummaryStudies have shown that brood parasites lay their eggs early in the egg-laying sequence of their hosts, providing them with the advantage of earlier hatching. However, common cuckoos (Cuculus canorus) appear to parasitize the nests of gray bushchat (Saxicola ferreus) during the late egg-laying stage.

pmc-10694726.title: Differences in Effort, Reward, Grit, Burnout, and Continuous Exercise Intention: Assessing the Effort-Reward Imbalance among Korean Athletes
pmc-10694726.creator: Inkyoung Park, Wi-Young So, Eui-Jae Lee
pmc-10694726.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Although studies have shown that an imbalance between effort and reward in the workplace negatively affects an individual’s physiological and mental health, few have looked at how this imbalance may affect the mental state of athletes. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the importance of the effort-reward imbalance (ERI) in athletes by examining whether psychological variables would differ depending on the ERI. To accomplish this, 795 registered collegiate athletes were recruited.

pmc-11425794.title: Selecting reasonable soil moisture-maintaining measures to improve the soil physicochemical properties and achieve high yield and quality of purple garlic in the China Hexi Corridor oasis agricultural area
pmc-11425794.creator: Xiaofan Pan, Hengjia Zhang, Haoliang Deng, Shouchao Yu, Chenli Zhou, Fuqiang Li
pmc-11425794.description: Agricultural plastic film, as an important agricultural production material in the China Hexi Corridor oasis agricultural area, is widely used in the intensive production process of purple garlic, which plays an important role in increasing yield, improving quality, ensuring supply, etc.

pmc-12613736.title: Contrasting organizational responses to femicide in Mexico’s public health crisis
pmc-12613736.creator: Veronica Valencia Gonzalez
pmc-12613736.description: BackgroundFemicide—the gender-motivated killing of women—remains an urgent public health and human rights crisis in Latin America. In Mexico, legal reforms have established formal mechanisms for prevention and response, yet implementation remains fragmented, particularly in regions marked by structural violence and institutional distrust.

pmc-12617493.title: Ist2 promotes lipid transfer by Osh6 via its membrane tethering and lipid scramblase activities
pmc-12617493.creator: Alicia Fabbre, Camille Syska, Heitor Gobbi Sebinelli, Anna Cardinal, Maud Magdeleine, Noha Al-Qatabi, Juan Martín D’Ambrosio, Cédric Montigny, Guillaume Lenoir, Alenka Čopič, Guillaume Drin
pmc-12617493.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Lipid transfer proteins unevenly distribute lipids within the cell, which is crucial for its functioning. In yeast, Osh6 transfers phosphatidylserine (PS) from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to the plasma membrane (PM) by exchange with phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate. We investigated why its activity depends on Ist2, an ER-resident lipid scramblase that connects the ER to the PM via an intrinsically disordered region (IDR).

pmc-12721802.title: Advances in the epigenetic regulation of breast cancer
pmc-12721802.creator: Xiao Liu, Xin Wu, Jianan Ding, Xiaoying Qiao, Jing Liang
pmc-12721802.description: The clonal evolution of breast cancer involves a complex dialogue between tumor cells and their environment. In this process, epigenetic mechanisms play a crucial role in regulating the cellular transcriptome without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Here, we provide an updated summary of three main epigenetic mechanisms: histone modifications, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and higher-order chromatin structures.

pmc-12748599.title: Historical insect disturbance maps from 1985 onwards for Canadian forests derived using earth observation data
pmc-12748599.creator: Pauline Perbet, Luc Guindon, David L. P. Correia, Omid Reisi Gahrouei, Jean-François Côté, Martin Béland
pmc-12748599.description: Despite the major impact of insect outbreaks on the Canadian boreal forest and its significance in carbon monitoring, current monitoring efforts primarily rely on costly and subjective aerial survey interpretations. While satellite remote sensing has been widely used to map wildfire and harvesting disturbances, no consistent, long-term dataset exists for severe canopy loss events in coniferous forests.

pmc-13139624.title: Acute Pancreatitis as an Extrahepatic Complication of Acute Hepatitis E Infection: A Case Report
pmc-13139624.creator: Syed Abdur Rehman Shah, Intikhab Alam, Syed Noman Ali Shah, Umaima Cheema, Aymar Akilimali
pmc-13139624.description: Clinicians should consider Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) a rare but significant etiology alongside established primary triggers, including gallstones and alcohol. Early HEV screening for hepatic and pancreatic dysfunction is required to improve care and avoid unnecessary interventions, especially in endemic regions. Introduction Acute pancreatitis is a common and potentially serious condition characterized by abrupt inflammation of the pancreas.

pmc-13180772.title: Life-Stage–Dependent Variation in Gastrointestinal Microbial Communities of Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-13180772.creator: Arnau Rocabert, Laia Pareras, Raquel Egea, Mohamed Alaraby, Laura Rubio, Ricard Marcos, Alba García-Rodríguez, Alba Hernández
pmc-13180772.description: Drosophila melanogaster has been a useful biological model since its first use, more than 100 years ago. Mainly due to its genetic similarity with humans, as it allowed it to be an accurate representation of how different biological systems work, such as immune function, illness related pathways, gene inheritance, egg development and, in this case, the microbial ecosystem.

pmc-13333628.title: Psychological safety in sport: validation of the French Sport Psychological Safety Inventory (SPSI-FR)
pmc-13333628.creator: Véronique Boudreault, Juliette Maurin, Lara Pomerleau-Fontaine, Charles-Anthony Dubeau, Francelyne Jean-Baptiste, Sophie Brassard, Jacinthe Dion, Sylvie Parent

pmc-13597185.title: Treatment switching in oncology evidence synthesis: a systematic review of meta-analytical practices incorporating time-dependent confounding, censoring bias, and patient-level variability
pmc-13597185.creator: Edward Kurnia Setiawan Limijadi
pmc-13597185.description: BackgroundTreatment switching in the oncology trials introduced time-dependent confounding and informative censoring, which complicated the unbiased estimation of treatment effects in evidence synthesis.ObjectivesTo systematically assess the meta-analytical practices that are used for adjusting treatment switching in oncology, with an emphasis on handling time-dependent confounding, censoring bias, as well as patient-level variability.MethodsA systematic review was conducted using PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

pmc-13669350.title: From association to causality: mechanistic pathways linking the gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders
pmc-13669350.creator: Sultan Almarzooqi, Lidya K. Yassin, Fatima Alnuaimi, Salma Alketbi, Jurga Skrabulyte-Barbulescu, Noud AlAhbabi, Dana Alremeithi, Rawdha Almarashda, Saif Almazrouei, Safa Shehab, Yauhen Statsenko, Mohammad I. K. Hamad
pmc-13669350.description: The microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) has emerged as a key framework for understanding how peripheral biological systems influence brain function and behaviour. However, despite extensive associative evidence linking gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders, robust causal and mechanistic insights remain limited. This review critically evaluates current evidence to determine whether microbiome alterations contribute to psychiatric pathophysiology and inform therapeutic strategies.
